purpose: Research-only evidence packet for five consecutive Dublin City NIAH candidates selected from the refreshed official missing-registration queue.

official_dataset_reference.title: NIAH Data Download
official_dataset_reference.coordinate_note: Official CSV ITM coordinates are EPSG:2157; CSV latitude/longitude are separate fields. Raw page coordinate pairs are preserved separately only where the individual NIAH page could be verified; otherwise they are explicitly unavailable.

candidate_records.address: 84 Marlborough Street / Cathedral Street, Dublin 1, Ireland
candidate_records.description_summary: Corner-sited three-bay three-storey house over basement, built c.1795, with replacement shopfronts to both elevations, Flemish-bond red brick walls, two-over-two timber sliding sash windows and a round-arched entrance with open-pedimented stucco surround.
candidate_records.appraisal_summary: NIAH describes a well-presented restored townhouse that provides scale and presence to the early streets and an appropriate setting for the Pro-Cathedral opposite.
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact registration 50010239 present in workflow #1995 Dublin City missing-registration queue.

candidate_records.description_summary: Terraced three-bay three-storey house over basement, built c.1795, formerly a pawnbroker's and recorded in the national CSV as restaurant use. NIAH's CSV description notes an M-profile hipped slate roof, Flemish-bond red brickwork, original sash windows and internal shutters, and an original wrought-iron pawnbroker's sign with three gilded balls.
candidate_records.appraisal_summary: NIAH describes a well-proportioned townhouse retaining early fenestration, internal shutters and an ornate original pawnbroker's sign, contributing to the intact streetscape.
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact registration 50010240 present in workflow #1995 Dublin City missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.source_access_caution: The official CSV entry and its full description were available in the workflow artifact. The individual record page could not be fetched by the browser during this review; its raw page coordinate pair is therefore not recorded. The official CSV values remain distinct and complete.

candidate_records.name: The Confession Box
candidate_records.description_summary: End-of-terrace two-bay four-storey house, built c.1800, with a c.1890 pub-front, ruled-and-lined rendered walls, moulded stucco details and an ornate Victorian shopfront with decorative lead dressing and gilded sign-writing.
candidate_records.appraisal_summary: NIAH records the former name The Maid of Erin and describes the building's association with Dionysius Lardner and the War of Independence-era confessions that gave rise to the name The Confession Box.
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact registration 50010241 present in workflow #1995 Dublin City missing-registration queue.

candidate_records.description_summary: Terraced four-bay four-storey stucco-fronted house, built c.1820 and now described as commercial premises, with ruled-and-lined render, timber sliding sash windows, decorative architraves and pedimented doorcases flanking a rendered shopfront.
candidate_records.appraisal_summary: NIAH notes the building's contribution to Marlborough Street's historic character, with graduated fenestration and decorative façade details.
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact registration 50010242 present in workflow #1995 Dublin City missing-registration queue.

candidate_records.name: Dunnes Stores
candidate_records.address: 23–24 Earl Street North / Cathedral Street, Dublin 1, Ireland
candidate_records.description_summary: Terraced six-bay four-storey stucco-fronted commercial building, built c.1920 and largely rebuilt c.2000, with timber shopfront, neoclassical stucco façade, and a substantial red-and-yellow brick rear block fronting Cathedral Street.
candidate_records.appraisal_summary: NIAH describes the building as part of the late nineteenth- and early twentieth-century commercial fabric around O'Connell Street; the lively stucco façade adds a decorative element to the streetscape.
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact registration 50010243 present in workflow #1995 Dublin City missing-registration queue.

identity_and_spatial_cautions: All five are distinct NIAH registrations and remain separate archive entities.
The national CSV NAME field is blank for 50010239, 50010240 and 50010242; do not invent names.

50010240's official CSV data and detailed description were present in the workflow artifact, but the individual page fetch failed during this review. Its raw page coordinates are intentionally null; do not infer them from CSV coordinates.
50010241 retains its exact CSV name The Confession Box; NIAH also records the previous name The Maid of Erin.

50010243 is a commercial building with an Earl Street North frontage and a rear block fronting Cathedral Street; retain as one NIAH registration unless future authoritative evidence indicates otherwise.
NIAH descriptions of use, condition and occupancy are survey-time statements, not present-day verification.
Raw page coordinate pairs are separate from official CSV ITM and latitude/longitude; never mix coordinate systems.
